bank.module: Session 9 — Pandas Fundamentals, DataFrames & Core Data Manipulation
bank.title: Python Session 9 — Production Bank 001

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Series` according to the taught session?

options.text: A Pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array that can hold data values.
A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table with columns that may have different types.
`head()` returns the first five rows by default for a quick preview.
`info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.

explanation.ar: A Pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array that can hold data values.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to create a one-dimensional labeled data structure?

options.text: pd.DataFrame(...)
pd.Series(...)
df.head()
df.info()

explanation.ar: `pd.Series(...)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: create a one-dimensional labeled data structure.

questions.question: A Series is most similar to what spreadsheet concept?

options.text: A complete workbook only
A filesystem directory
A single column
A Python loop

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `Series` behavior: A Pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array that can hold data values.

questions.question: A learner uses a two-dimensional DataFrame when the requirement is specifically a one-dimensional labeled structure. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `pd.DataFrame(...)` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `Series` has no rules.
Convert the task to `head()` without changing the logic.
Use a Series for one-dimensional labeled data.

explanation.ar: Use a Series for one-dimensional labeled data.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `DataFrame` according to the taught session?

options.text: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table with columns that may have different types.
`head()` returns the first five rows by default for a quick preview.
`info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.
`describe()` generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns such as mean, standard deviation, min and max.

explanation.ar: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table with columns that may have different types.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to create a two-dimensional table?

options.text: df.head()
pd.DataFrame(...)
df.info()
df.describe()

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. `pd.DataFrame(...)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: create a two-dimensional table.

questions.question: What does the source compare a DataFrame to?

options.text: A set with no columns
A text file object
A table in a database or a data frame in R
A scalar only

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `DataFrame` behavior: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table with columns that may have different types.

questions.question: A learner expects a DataFrame to behave as an unordered set with no columns. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `df.head()` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `DataFrame` has no rules.
Convert the task to `info()` without changing the logic.
Treat it as a labeled two-dimensional table.

explanation.ar: Treat it as a labeled two-dimensional table.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `head()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `head()` returns the first five rows by default for a quick preview.
`info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.
`describe()` generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns such as mean, standard deviation, min and max.

options.text: df.info()
df.head()
df.describe()
df["column"] / df[condition]

questions.question: How many rows does `head()` return by default in the taught description?

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `head()` behavior: `head()` returns the first five rows by default for a quick preview.

questions.question: A learner loads a full summary when only a quick first-row preview is needed. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `df.info()` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `head()` has no rules.
Convert the task to `describe()` without changing the logic.
Use `head()` for the quick top-of-data preview taught.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `info()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.
`describe()` generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns such as mean, standard deviation, min and max.
Selecting a column returns a Series; Boolean conditions can filter rows.

explanation.ar: `info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to inspect non-null counts and dtypes?

options.text: df.describe()
df.info()
df["column"] / df[condition]
df.loc[...]

explanation.ar: `df.info()` is the course-aligned choice for this task: inspect non-null counts and dtypes.

questions.question: Which detail is explicitly provided by `info()`?

options.text: Only mean salary
Only sorted rows
Data types and non-null counts

questions.question: Which statement best describes `describe()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `describe()` generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns such as mean, standard deviation, min and max.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to summarize numerical columns statistically?

options.text: df["column"] / df[condition]
df.describe()
df.loc[...]
df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. `df.describe()` is the course-aligned choice for this task: summarize numerical columns statistically.

questions.question: Which statistic is part of the taught describe output?

Directory owner
Mean
Map marker

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `describe()` behavior: `describe()` generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns such as mean, standard deviation, min and max.

questions.question: A learner uses `head()` expecting mean/std/min/max. What correction best matches the course?

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Column Selection & Filtering` according to the taught session?

options.text: Selecting a column returns a Series; Boolean conditions can filter rows.
`loc[]` is label-based indexing for selecting specific rows and columns.
Pandas supports adding columns, vectorized column updates, and dropping columns with `drop(..., axis=1)`.
`isnull()` detects missing values, `fillna()` fills them, and `dropna()` removes rows with missing values.

explanation.ar: Selecting a column returns a Series; Boolean conditions can filter rows.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to select a column or filter matching rows?

options.text: df.loc[...]
df["column"] / df[condition]
df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)
isnull()/fillna()/dropna()

explanation.ar: `df["column"] / df[condition]` is the course-aligned choice for this task: select a column or filter matching rows.

questions.question: What does selecting one DataFrame column normally return?

options.text: A directory
A tuple of files
A Series
A scalar always

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `Column Selection & Filtering` behavior: Selecting a column returns a Series; Boolean conditions can filter rows.

questions.question: A learner creates a Boolean condition but forgets to use it to filter the DataFrame. What correction best matches the course?

options.text: Use `df.loc[...]` instead regardless of the goal.
Ignore the issue because `Column Selection & Filtering` has no rules.

explanation.ar: Apply the condition inside DataFrame selection to return matching rows.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `loc[]` according to the taught session?

options.text: `loc[]` is label-based indexing for selecting specific rows and columns.

`isnull()` detects missing values, `fillna()` fills them, and `dropna()` removes rows with missing values.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Modify DataFrame` according to the taught session?

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Missing Data` according to the taught session?
